newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND MOVE SIX POINTS CLEAR IN SHEFFIELD SHIELD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND MOVE SIX POINTS CLEAR IN SHEFFIELD SHIELD.

text.p: Trevor Barsby hit a composed 68
on Monday to steer Queensland to a seven wicket win over New
South Wales and a six point lead at the top of the Sheffield
Shield table.
Chasing 108 to win, Queensland reached their victory target
for the loss of three wickets and now lead the standings with a
maximum 12 points from two games with New South Wales and
Tasmania in joint second place.
Tasmania, who have struggled in recent seasons, recorded a
rare win for a visiting team in Perth by beating Western
Australia by 141 runs.
In a third match completed on Monday, Victoria beat South
Australia by nine wickets but have only 5.7 points to their
credit after being penalised 0.3 points for a slow over rate in
their previous match.
New South Wales were thoroughly outplayed despite the
presence of
test captain Mark Taylor and the Waugh twins Steve and Mark.
Only Steve Waugh, who scored a century in the first innings,
made any impact against a Queensland attack that included
Australia test newcomer Michael Kasprowicz.
Kasprowicz celebrated his selection for the first test
against West Indies, starting in Brisbane on Friday, with match
figures of six for 128.
In Melbourne, all-rounder Ian Harvey snared seven for 44 to
help Victoria to a comfortable win.
